data.name: Beat Boxer
data.detailed_description:
Exercise to your own music! Punch, dodge, and dance around the ring.

BeatBoxer is a VR boxing game that puts you in the spotlight of your own boxing match. Play any song from Youtube or use Airplay to play a continuous stream of music from Spotify, Pandora, iTunes, or your favorite music app.

Train up from a feather weight, to world champ with increasing difficulty. Dip left and right to avoid dodges while executing upper cuts and jabs to the rhythm of your music. Immerse yourself and dance around the ring in Room-Scale VR. Put your opponent on the ropes and connect multiple streaks to increase your score.

Each song is generated in real time using our custom developed music analysis software that
Allows you to stream continuously from any Airplay device – or directly from Youtube.

BeatBoxer tracks your score in a local leaderboard so you can show your friends who really floats like a butter fly and stings like a bee.

Active developers on this project mean that new features are pumped out rapidly and community feedback molds new features.

reviews.review:
I'm really really sad to give a "Not Recommended" rating to this game. I suspect I will be able to change it as my only issues are bugs/performance issues. I won this game in a Reddit giveaway (thanks to the dev!!) and I'm excited to play this once it is polished up a little more.

TL;DR: Games that I can get into are SUPER fun!! Unfortunately with all the crashes it isn't worth the struggle.

Pros:
--Beat Mapping feels pretty great. I've only been able to play about 4 songs (I'll address this in cons), but they all felt pretty good on the 2nd and 3rd difficulties. 
--The 4 color options really make the game feel more intense than others like Audioshield where you just have to match up left/right hand. Adding more to the mental aspect of the game is huge added value (and challenge) for me.
--Dodge is great! Really engages your whole body which is excellent for added challenge as well as your cardiovascular fitness! Part of the reason I play Audioshield is to get a bit of a workout and I can say that this game got me sweating more than Audioshield ever does after just a few songs. For comparison I play Audioshield on "elite" difficulty.
--360 degrees of play is awesome. Adds to the physical aspect and this simple additon exponentially increases the fun! Only downside of this is it is easy to get tangled up in the Vive cord.
--Point mutipliers. You should be rewarded with more points for doing well and the cheering and big sign saying you increased your multiplier is motivating to kick even more butt!

Cons:
--The first few times I tried playing this it made me SICK. The intro screen where you select your music source locks up so when you move your head the entire screen moves around with you rather than looking around in the environment. The first several times I played the game it locked up here, crashed, and I was unable to get in. I tried a few more times over the last month with no luck. I was finally able to get into some games today. Still had the same problem, but if I wait a minute or two it fixes itself. Even bigger problem is that when you try to search or sort by music genre in the YouTube menu the same thing happens and it takes several minutes to load or it crashes.
--FREQUENT CRASHES. My system is pretty well able to run any VR stuff on the market (MSI R9 390, top end i5 processor, and 16 gigs of RAM) but the game crashes any time I give input. If I'm lucky I can get a game in.
--Inconsistent haptic feedback. When it works, it feels great. In rhythym gaming you absolutely need haptic feedback when you hit notes/orbs. Unfotunately sometimes it just doesn't work. I thought maybe at first I was just missing notes (Note: there is also nothing to tell you when you miss a note other than your multiplier going back to 1x) but I would hit notes that bring up the next level of the multiplier with no haptic feedback. Definitely am hitting those. 

All in all, if the dev can fix the crashing and freezing I will overwhelmingly recommend the game. Until then the existing issues are unforgivable. I will try playing some more games now that I have gotten it to work.
